title: v1/chat: session param mapping, stream coalescing and envelope-normalized stop/logprobs
author: Sophie Nguyen
description:
Summary: Add full parity support for several /v1/chat.completions behaviors used by OpenAI-compatible clients: 1) map and persist incoming 'session' metadata and new session.* params into request context for routing/metrics; 2) normalize stop parameter precedence with a new stop_policy (explicit arrays, string fallback, stop_priority), preserving exact semantics expected by downstream tool callers; 3) keep logprobs block as a first-class envelope field in streaming chunks (no interleaving with text tokens) to allow incremental logprob aggregation; 4) implement a stream event coalescer that reduces tiny heartbeat-only frames and groups adjacent token->toolcall transitions to improve client stability and reduce network chatter; 5) tighten the function/tool-call handshake framing so the runtime only emits a single framed TOOL_CALL_START event per logical call and guarantees TOOL_CALL_END with idempotent retry semantics. Motivation: customers integrating with OpenAI-compatible SDKs ran into corner cases where session-level metadata was lost across retries, stop semantics differed between the Redwood v1 adapter and client expectations, streaming clients had difficulty consuming micro-frames which led to flakiness for low-latency workloads, and some tool-calling sequences produced duplicate partial events under high concurrency. This PR addresses those problems and adds tests and docs.
Changes in this PR:
- new mapping layer: server/adapter/chat_v1_session.py that maps session and session.* params to internal RequestContext and tags telemetry; ensures deterministic hashing for routing and warm-cache reuse
- stop normalizer: server/adapter/stop_policy.py with unit tests that implement precedence: explicit_stop_array > stop_string_list (legacy) > model_default; also supports stop_priority: longest_first|first_match
- streaming envelope: runtime/stream/envelope.proto + runtime/stream/envelope_writer.cpp implementing "logprob_envelope" blocks that can be emitted as separate events; client SDKs updated to expect envelope events during streaming
- coalescer: runtime/stream/coalescer.cpp + tests that batch small events (<1ms apart) into a single websocket/frame payload when safe and within latency SLO
- toolcall framing: runtime/tool_call/handshake.h/.cpp and server/adapter/toolcall_adapter.py updated to ensure idempotent start/end markers and a retry-safe call id
- SDK adapters: sdk/python/openai_compat.py and sdk/typescript/openai_compat.ts updated to surface session param and envelope parsing
- docs: docs/openai_compat_v1.md updated with migration notes and examples
- tests: integration tests added under tests/integration/test_chat_v1_session.py and several new e2e playback fixtures.
Description/Checklist:
- Context and design rationale included in the top-level docstring of chat_v1_session.py
- Backwards compatible defaults: stop_policy defaults to legacy behavior unless customer enablement flag set
- Add unit and integration tests covering: stop arrays, stop strings, logprob envelope aggregation, websocket coalesce thresholds, toolcall retry scenarios
- Performance: coalescer is opt-in via runtime flag and disabled for Dedicated plans by default
- Docs and SDKs updated
- Linear references included below
Testing summary:
- Local unit test suite: all green
- Integration matrix (linux/gcc, macos) run in CI; initial CI run failed on a flaky websocket test and was retried; stabilized after increasing default coalesce timeout in the test harness (see CI section).
Migration notes (short):
- Customers relying on exact token-level interleaving for logprobs must opt into legacy "raw_token_stream" mode; default is now envelope-separated logprobs for stability
- Session param is purely additive: it will appear in telemetry and routing but does not change model selection unless customers configure routing rules

release_notes:
- Add session param mapping for v1/chat to persist metadata and facilitate routing.
- Introduce stop_policy normalizer to align stop semantics with OpenAI-compatible clients.
- Stream logprobs as a dedicated envelope event for stable incremental aggregation.
- Opt-in stream coalescer to reduce micro-frame noise and improve client stability.
- Improved toolcall handshake framing to avoid duplicate partial events and make retries idempotent.
